name: Likum
confidence_why: Blust 2021, the only description of Likum, says outright that stress was recorded only early in elicitation and that it remains unclear whether it is penultimate or initial, and Blust's 1975 fieldnotes say nothing about stress, so the catalog's 'undetermined' rests on a single first-hand source with nothing to contradict it.
catalog_citation: Blust, Robert. 2021. Sketch 5: Likum. In: Eight Languages of the Admiralty Islands, Papua New Guinea. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia, LLM Special Issue 2021. Linguistic Society of Papua New Guinea (www.langlxmelanesia.com).
catalog_quote: Stress was recorded in the early stages of elicitation, but not thereafter. In isolation word stress appeared to be relatively even on the penultimate and final syllables, with no evidence of contrast. In bimorphemic trisyllables such as /co-hahu/ ‘six’, or /co-rueh/ ‘eight’, stress was recorded on the penult, but in the monomorphemic trisyllable /asihen/ ‘sneeze’, it was recorded on the first syllable. Stress was not recorded for other polysyllables, and it consequently remains unclear whether the stress is penultimate or initial in phrasal context. I have transcribed it here as uniformly penultimate.

audit.reasoning: The classification 'undetermined' rests on the only existing description of Likum (Blust 2021 grammar sketch, phonology section), which we hold in full; the deciding quotation is verbatim at the cited page and section, and the author explicitly states that it 'remains unclear whether the stress is penultimate or initial' and that penultimate marking is a transcription convention only. No better or competing source exists (Glottolog: zero other descriptive refs; the sketch is mis-typed there as a wordlist). Coding and strength of the evidence stand; no action needed.
